messages:
Anna (oncall): paging: noticed a surge of streaming SSE disconnects affecting function-calling routes (tool-call responses truncated). Customers in eu-west reporting errors. throwing this into incidents channel for triage. thread_ts=1775001111
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: 1775001111 - high-error-rate on /v1/stream/function-call (SSE). Pages sent to oncall. Impact: streaming clients see 'parse_error' or abrupt close. Automated mitigations: disabled canary model variant for streaming.
Anna (oncall): quick summary: at ~2026-06-18T12:04Z we started seeing elevated SSE disconnects and "tool-call parsing error" logs. Traffic spike + streaming drops. Not a full outage but high error rates for customers using streaming tool-calls (esp. eu-west).
Sam K: on it. which infra team should I loop? infra-runtime or eng-runtime?
Anna (oncall): loop eng-runtime + infra-sre. Maria, can you pull any kube/host-level OOMs or network flaps around 12:00-12:20Z?
Maria L: grabbing logs now. posting earliest signs below.
Maria L: TIMELINE NOTE: 12:02: small traffic increase from partner A (burst). 12:05: spike of 5xx-codec-errors in runtime logs. 12:07: first SSE disconnects seen in ELB logs (RST from server side). 12:10: bulk of errors between 12:08-12:18. no node reboots.
Infra SRE Bot: host metrics (eu-west-3) snapshot: cpu spikes on pod redwood-runtime-23 (p90 cpu 92%), network retransmits up ~3x. No recent kube deployments in that window.
Sam K: ok eng-runtime, hypothesis: streaming frames too large (tool-call result contains big JSON with embeddings or trace) and the SSE connection handling code is choking and closing. Could also be client incompatibility with new structured-tool payloads.
Devex Blake: FYI we rolled out a small structured-tool change yesterday that included an extra top-level metadata array in tool responses. Might be relevant for client parsers.
Anna (oncall): let's triage hypotheses systematically. I'll capture hypotheses here and mark evidence as we get it. H1: Server-side SSE framing bug triggered by large frames -> evidence: high cpu on runtime pod, 'write: broken pipe' in runtime logs. H2: Client parser incompatibility with new tool metadata -> evidence: partner A logs show parse failure string 'unexpected token \"meta\" at position 0'. H3: Network layer (load balancer) closing idle streaming connections due to increased retransmits -> evidence: ELB logs show RST from backend.
QA Bot: adding reproduction checklist: 1) reproduce streaming function-call with large tool response; 2) run curl SSE client and observe disconnects; 3) collect runtime debug logs with TRACE.
Sam K: live mitigation proposal: 1) enable server-side fallback to non-streaming (chunked polling) for affected customers 2) reduce tool payload size by stripping metadata on the fly for streaming route 3) enforce smaller SSE frame size (chunk responses). Which is fastest?
Anna (oncall): 1 + 2 are fastest. Maria, can you enable non-streaming fallback for partner A and a few high-volume tenants? We have a toggle: feature.flag.streaming_fallback -> true for tenant ids.
Maria L: toggled fallback for tenants: partner-A, tenant-334, enterprise-x. Verified lower error-rate for partner-A within 3m.
Infra SRE Bot: mitigation applied: traffic rerouted to non-streaming endpoints for flagged tenants. No infra-level config changes needed.
Sam K: while mitigation is in place, let's collect concrete examples of failing payloads. Anna, can you ask partner A to share a sample session id?
Anna (oncall): asked partner A; they sent session id: sess_20260618_92ab. Partner's client logs show: "parse_error at bytes 0-12" and then immediate connection close.
Devex Blake: posting a reproduction curl (useful for eng-runtime):
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/function-call?session=sess_20260618_92ab"
```
Expected: SSE events with tool-call JSON. Observed: connection closes after first large chunk, then client receives partial event ending mid-json.
Sam K: eng-runtime, please grep for 'write: broken pipe' and 'parse_error' around timeframe. Also capture full request/response sizes for the failing requests.
Anna (oncall): eng-runtime (Sam), infra-sre (Maria) to coordinate log bundle upload to /artifacts/incidents/1775001111/. Post links here when available.
Maria L: uploaded runtime logs snippet: https://internal.redwood/s3/incidents/1775001111/runtime_pod_23.log (excerpt below)
```
[12:06:54Z] WARN stream_writer.go:204 write chunk failed: write tcp 10.2.3.5:443->10.10.1.5:52344: write: broken pipe
[12:06:54Z] ERROR tool_parse.go:87 parse error: unexpected token "meta" at position 1, payload_size=238764
[12:07:01Z] INFO connection.go: keepalive sent
[12:07:02Z] WARN connection.go: retransmit count increased
```
Sam K: evidence leans H1+H2: large payloads + changed metadata combine to cause server write to block and then close. Need to confirm whether the runtime's SSE writer blocks on socket write for large frames and then triggers connection close.
Anna (oncall): assigning: Sam K -> debug SSE writer path (non-blocking writes? buffer limits?), Maria L -> network trace from ELB -> backend for failing requests, Devex Blake -> provide exact schema change from yesterday. QA Bot -> attempt repro with downlevel client that doesn't expect 'meta' array.
QA Bot: repro attempt: downlevel client v1.4.2 fails consistently when payload > 200KB and contains 'meta' array. Attached minimal repro payload: https://internal.redwood/s3/incidents/1775001111/repro_payload.json
Sam K: found relevant code: stream_writer.go uses a 64KB buffer and falls back to blocking writes when buffered. If payload > 64KB we see backpressure and eventual broken pipe if client cannot accept data fast enough. That explains the 'write: broken pipe' and partial JSON delivered.
Devex Blake: confirmed schema diff: yesterday's change added top-level metadata array in responses for tool-call v2. Example: "metadata": [ {"source":"trace","size":...}, ... ]. Some client parsers assume first token is object key for tool result and choke on array insertion.
Anna (oncall): putting a quick combed hypothesis ranking: Primary root cause = server-side buffering/backpressure interactions + incompatible client assumptions about top-level shape = streaming tool-call parse failures. Secondary contributor = traffic burst amplified backpressure.
Sam K: short-term fix implemented: 1) Strip metadata for streaming responses (server side) -> deployed at 12:45Z. 2) Increase stream_writer buffer to 256KB to avoid immediate blocking. 3) Marked rollback for structured-tool change in canary.
Maria L: monitoring shows error-rate dropped ~90% for flagged tenants after strip/deploy. Non-flagged customers still low level of errors; increasing buffer further may help.
Anna (oncall): impact notes: affected customers: partner-A (eu-west), tenant-334, enterprise-x. Customer-visible symptom: SSE connection closed mid-event, client parse_error. No data corruption reported; most clients retried and recovered. No PII exposure.
Incident Bot: Note: page created and escalated. Postmortem required. Owner: Sam K. Severity: Sev2. First response at 12:06Z. Mitigation at 12:45Z.
Devex Blake: action items for RCA: - full timeline (who deployed what when) - reproduce and fix stream_writer non-blocking behaviour - define compatibility policy for schema changes on streaming endpoints - add integration tests for large SSE frames
Sam K: I'll own the RCA. I'll gather code pointers and add timeline. Maria please attach the full ELB logs and pod-level netstat dumps. QA, please add a regression test that simulates 250KB tool payloads.
QA Bot: started regression job #1775001111-repro. will report pass/fail in 30m.
Anna (oncall): handoff: I'm going offline in 20m. Sam, you're next oncall lead for the incident cleanup and RCA. Please keep stakeholder updates to affected customers. I'll update support notes before I go.
Sam K: taking lead. I'll open the internal RCA doc and post link here. Preliminary RCA doc: https://docs.redwood/internal/incidents/1775001111-rca (will populate).
Maria L: uploaded ELB logs + netstat: https://internal.redwood/s3/incidents/1775001111/elb_netstat_bundle.tar.gz
Anna (oncall): thanks team. final note for now: mitigation worked, monitoring still watchful, tagging postmortem as P0->P2 per impact. If anything regresses, re-open the page. :thumbsup:
Sam K: noted — continuing work. will ping when RCA draft ready.
